newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends shade up on bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends shade up on bargain hunting.

text.p: The Hong Kong gold market ended a tad above New York's Wednesday close after very slow trade marked largely by bargain hunting from physical buyers, dealers and traders said on Thursday.
"We only saw small bargain hunting from physical users," said a gold dealer at a large bullion bank.
Bullion ended at US$368.70/369.20 an ounce against New York's US$368.60/369.10 close on Wednesday.
Traders saw continued selling interest at $371 and said the market was well supported at $368.
"This is why things will remain range-bound," said one dealer.
One large bank reported selling interest from Europe.
"It's probably producer-related," the dealer at the bank said.
Dealers forecast gold to stay at current levels unless players who were short started covering their positions to square up books at the end of the year.
Local tael gold was still trading at a premium to spot gold, with the U.S. dollar equivalent at $369.20/70.
Some dealers said that earlier positive carryover charges at the local gold exchange had forced people to buy tael gold to earn interest.
Local gold ended HK$2 lower at HK$3,405 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -6.0 from its previous fix at -7.0.
